title: Auxiliary Power Unit Mount Inspections Are Taking Too Long and Finding Too Much — Request for a Better Standard
abstract: Karoo Skyways asks for the auxiliary power unit mounting standard to be improved after finding worn bushes and elongated holes at the aft mount on aircraft that already carry the current improved link.

sections.request: We are opening the tail cone every six thousand hours to look at the auxiliary power unit mounts and we do not like what we are finding. On five of our aircraft the aft mount bushes are worn past the limit and on two of them the bolt holes in the link have started to go oval. All of these aircraft already have the improved link fitted, so this is not the old problem coming back, it is something else. Our people also tell us the inspection itself is difficult because you cannot get a proper look at the aft link without dropping the heat shield, which turns a two hour job into a shift. We use the auxiliary power unit heavily because our ground infrastructure is limited, so we accept that our aircraft work it harder than most, but we would like a mount that copes with that rather than an inspection that finds the damage after it has happened.
sections.background: Seven findings on twelve aircraft over four years, all at the aft mount and all on aircraft with the improved link standard already embodied. Average auxiliary power unit running hours on our fleet are roughly 1.8 times the fleet average because we run it on the ground at three of our four bases. The heat shield removal adds about six hours to every inspection and we do the inspection eight times a year across the fleet.
sections.expected_outcome: A mount arrangement that survives our utilisation between heavy checks, and an inspection that can be done without dropping the heat shield. If the answer is a further improved link we would want it to fit the aircraft we have already modified without a second round of hole rework.

type_data.business_justification: Seven aft mount findings on aircraft already at the improved standard, with six hours of heat shield removal added to every inspection and eight inspections a year across the fleet.
